question: A Canadian landlord asks for my SIN as identification on a routine rental application. Does Service Canada guidance say I must provide it?
generated_answer:
The Service Canada guidance states that you should only provide your SIN when required by law. Rental applications are not typically considered a legal requirement for providing your SIN. You can politely decline to provide it and suggest alternative forms of identification, such as a driver's license or passport. If the landlord insists, you may want to consider looking for another rental property where the landlord is more respectful of your privacy and the law. Remember, your SIN is sensitive personal information and should be protected. 

For more information, you can refer to the Service Canada website: [https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/when-to-provide-your-social-insurance-number.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/when-to-provide-your-social-insurance-number.html) 

If you feel that your privacy rights are being violated, you can also contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada for guidance: [https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/](https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/) 

Always prioritize your personal information security and privacy. 

**Note:** This response is based on general guidance and may not cover all possible scenarios or legal interpretations. If you have specific concerns or questions, it's always best to consult with a legal professional or the relevant authorities directly. 

**Update (2023):** As of 2023, the guidance from Service Canada and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada remains consistent with the information provided above. However, it's always a good idea to check the most current resources for the latest advice and any changes in regulations or laws. 

**Additional Tip:** If you do decide to provide your SIN for a rental application, ensure you understand how the landlord will protect and store this information to prevent identity theft or unauthorized use. 

**Final Note:** This response is for informational purposes only and should not be considered legal advice. Always consult with a legal professional for advice tailored to your specific situation.
